maya: quick heads-up — after landing the fused-epilogue + qkv-pack change on canary we see a p99 regression for long sequences (seq=1024+). attaching profiler traces and a tiny repro. @jon can you take a look?

jon: saw that on my runs too. p50 roughly unchanged but p99 jumped ~35% on A100 tests. batch=1, seq=1536: before=42ms p99, after=57ms p99. cpu-side queuing looks fine. nvprof shows spikes in L2 misses during the epilogue stage.

maya: repro command i used: 
```
./bench_runner --model redwood-test/gpt-small --kernel fused_qkv_pack --epilogue fused_bias_rope --seq 1536 --bs 1 --kv-mode paged --iters 200
```
outputs + traces uploaded to /artifacts/fused-epilogue/3055551234/

sasha: looked at telemetry — kvcache_page_faults metric jumped by ~4x when epilogue fusion is on. seems we allocate a small temp buffer per head that touches pages across the KV allocator boundary. on paged-kv that forces extra page loads, which explains L2/memory blowups.

kevin: ugh. that matches a suspicion i had — epilogue was doing head-parallel postproc and did an atomic write into a shadow buffer before folding into kv pages. on normal contiguous KV that’s cheap, but with paged allocator page-crossing kills locality.

jon: quick numbers from perf:
- baseline (packed qkv off, epilogue separate): p50=38ms p99=42ms bandwidth=650 GB/s util
- fused pack + fused epilogue: p50=40ms p99=57ms bandwidth=420 GB/s util
so peak bandwidth drops while stalls / cache-miss cycles up.

maya: i profiled at kernel level: epilogue does 3 memcpy-like ops per head that are strided. two of them hit nonresident pages on paged-kv. nvtx/time ranges attached.

kevin: short-term mitigation options:
1) change kernel chooser to prefer non-packed fused-attn for seq>1024 when kv-mode==paged
2) add a page-aware epilogue path that merges writes into the destination page-wise (more complex)
3) fall back to per-token epilogue (older code) for paged-kv

maya: i prototyped option (1) locally; switching kernel chooser rule eliminates the p99 regression but gives up some p50 wins for mid sequences. probably safest for canary.

sasha: also worth noting: our batching heuristics increase continuous sequence lengths for some workloads when the new kernel is allowed — that made the regression more visible in real traffic. we should tweak the batcher to cap fused-attn candidate seq growth while we iterate.

jon: agree. operational plan:
- roll kernel-chooser override to canary pool (kevin) — immediate
- instrument epilogue to track page-cross writes (maya + sasha) — do in next PR
- evaluate page-aware epilogue design (research spike, kevin) — 1 week spike

kevin: creating canary override patch now. will post PR link and deploy bot will show status.

infra-bot: deploy requested by kevin: patch/kernel-chooser/canary-override -> canary cluster. CI queued. (logs: https://ci.redwood.local/1234)

maya: thanks. i also dumped a small microbench that measures per-head write-set and page touches; will upload and add to perf regression suite.

jon: one more datapoint — models with rotary-only (no bias) see smaller regressions; bias+rope fusion path tends to allocate extra temp for bias addition. makes sense to gate bias fusion behind page-awareness.

sasha: noted. i'll add a telemetry flag: `epilogue_bias_fusion_page_throttle` so we can turn it off quickly if needed.

kevin: thanks team. if canary looks good we'll push chooser override and keep working on a proper epilogue rewrite. low-risk route first. :thumbsup:

maya: filing follow-ups:
- PERF-1423: page-aware epilogue design doc (maya)
- PERF-1424: kernel-chooser long-seq paged-kv rule (kevin)
- PERF-1425: batcher cap for fused-attn candidate (sasha)
links will be in the thread when i create them.

jon: sounds good. i put the nvprof trace and a small flamegraph in the artifacts dir. folks can repro with the command above.

kevin: PR linked: https://git.redwood/internal/pull/9812 — patch includes chooser rule + test matrix.

maya: ok leaving this open — will check canary numbers after infra finishes deploy.

infra-bot: deploy succeeded: canary cluster updated (revision abc123) at 3055551267

jon: after override landed, canary p99 back within 3% of baseline on our test harness. closing loop for immediate incident.

sasha: continuing with telemetry and batcher change. will report back by EOD tomorrow.

maya: great. thanks everyone.
